label: early original-phase k/t/2/o after j/k/3-like token
explanation: Fires almost only on original-phase input at positions 1-3. Position 2 holds 68% of the activation mass. It never fires at t=0 or t>=5, and almost never at the delimiter or in the copy phase. Within that window it is selective for the current token: k, t, 2 and o carry about 80% of the mass, with weaker firing on p, r, j and 3. It is strongest when an earlier input is one of j, k, 3, h, p, 2, v or u (top examples: j j [k], 3 j [t], 3 k [t]). The position window alone gets 99% recall but 4% precision. Adding the token sets raises dev F1 to about 0.53, but which current/previous token pairs fire still looks like a conjunctive lookup table over specific pairs that a simple predicate does not capture.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=1: k, t, 2, o; t=3: k, t, 2, o; t=2: k, t, 2, o) and the previous input (most: j, k, 3, p, h, 2; least: s, w, m, 0); timing cues that raise it most: t=2, t=3, L=3 & t=5.
